facts.text: Find the treasure shown on the party's treasure map.
Where are the locations marked on the treasure map, and which of them holds the treasure?
Reginald the Frog warns that a little trickster called a Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into Brandonsford every night, up to no good, and that the party should stay away from wherever it goes.
What is the Clurichen doing when it comes into Brandonsford from the riverbanks each night?
Kill the black dragon near Brandonsford and drag its body into town to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold bounty.
George, a capable woodsman living a couple of houses from the Clumsy Fox who lost an arm to the dragon, could tell the party about his encounter; Eric says he might show up at the tavern tonight.
Lady Hilda offers to join the party for pay on the dragon hunt.
Where did this black dragon come from, when Sir Brandon's dragon was killed and torn apart centuries ago?
A black dragon, not a big one per George, roams outside Brandonsford; it tore off George's arm, and Gill's three sons are out hunting it now.
Lady Hilda, a seasoned-looking noblewoman with chain mail and a shield, offers to join the party for money for the dragon hunt; she says she cannot kill the dragon herself, and no fee has been named.
Sir Phidipaldi told Lady Hilda the party would talk with Eric the Reeve and come back to her to take up her services.

Drop Dead Ned, a thief with a killer wasp in a jar on his necklace, offers himself and the wasp for hire at 100 gold a week, as long as he gets to kill people with the wasp. For a night of at least ten kills, he would give back 5 gold per kill if he can do what he wants with the bodies. Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.
What happened to Brandonsford's restocking shipment, due a week ago, and why have no goods reached town in months?
Dunk is weighing acquiring Farmer Gill's shabby prize mule, Shamus, which Gill suggests would let him start his own farm.
Farmer Gill offers to sell Shamus to Dunk for 100 gold.
When Dunk asked to trade work for Shamus, Gill said the big work needed was killing the dragon outside town; no deal was agreed.
Gill says Warwick the smith displays a beautiful mithril chain shirt, probably the best in the world, which would fit a normal-sized person but not Dunk; Warwick always refuses to sell it.
Why is Warwick growing more paranoid and covering his shop in lucky charms and clovers? Gill thinks it is to keep away Ingrid the potion seller, who fancies him.
Sir Phidipaldi agreed to help Quinn get back at Bentley, whom Quinn blames for stealing his ale at night; Quinn promised him 100 gold for that help.

Sir Phidipaldi agreed to stage a fake ale delivery at the Golden Egg: Quinn brings up bottles, they fill them with water, and Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of coming in to deliver them, to see what happens.
What empties or knocks over Quinn's stock every night at the Golden Egg? Quinn blames Bentley.
